key_idea: The 100000th prime is 1299709, so sieve to 1.3M, walk primes by index and test decimal substring containment.
sketch: Sieve of Eratosthenes up to 1,300,000, counting primes as they appear; for indices in [l,h] convert the prime to a string and use find with p read as a string (so leading zeros are preserved). O(N log log N + h*7). Pitfall: p must be read as a string, not an integer, because '00' differs from '0'; each prime is counted once regardless of the number of occurrences.
